Universe, ranking and limitations

Each venue is limited to the 16 highest-volume supported instruments that have a related peer. Pairs share a predefined industry or asset group and the same contract type. Symbols are matched exactly; the universe is not exhaustive. Each instrument’s history is fetched once per scan and shared across its pairs.

Rank uses the last 240 matched 5-minute bars: 35% return-correlation stability across two halves, 25% closeness of an AR(1) residual half-life estimate to 30 minutes, 20% estimated spread move versus trading friction, and 20% minimum-leg 24-hour notional volume. This heuristic is not a probability, cointegration test or expected return.

Passing requires current completed candles, at least 240 matched bars, no more than two gaps, at most 20% unchanged-price bars, an open session, recent quotes where timestamps exist, correlation ≥ 0.5 overall and ≥ 0.3 in each half, estimated half-life 5–120 minutes, and estimated spread move ≥ 2× estimated round-trip friction. A divergence flag additionally requires |z| between 1.5 and 3 with the same sign on 15-minute context.

Friction uses hedge-weighted reported taker fees and bid/ask spreads, plus the slippage assumption. Funding, market impact and liquidation risk are excluded. Missing costs keep a pair in research-only status. Arcus history uses oracle prices and lacks bid/ask data here. Variational has no verified history in this integration and appears only as a liquidity watchlist. No pair is forced to qualify.

How the test works

Each signal fits log(A) = α + β × log(B) using only the preceding bars. Entries and signal exits fill at the next observed close. Entry β, mean and standard deviation stay fixed during the trade. Positive β between 0 and 10 is required. Dollar allocations are gross/(1+β) and gross×β/(1+β), with opposite signs.

The optional confirmation uses complete 15-minute buckets and a 20-bar fit. Positions close at the final available bar of each UTC date, assuming that session boundary is known; no position carries to the next date. Gaps within a date can delay execution. No leverage, margin, partial fills or liquidation model. Z-score and correlation do not establish cointegration. Results use the entire selected sample; there is no out-of-sample validation.

What the scanner measures

The 5-minute z-score compares the latest log-price residual with a fit over the preceding 60 bars. Return correlation uses those recent 5-minute returns. The 15-minute view uses complete 15-minute buckets and 20 prior bars. A large divergence is a research flag, not a validated entry signal. Liquidity and actual funding history are not included in scanner rankings.

Demo prices are generated, not downloaded from any venue. Imported data is user-supplied and labelled by your selected source. All timestamps are displayed in UTC.
